name: microduck
one_liner: A small, buyable robot duck (about the size of a cat) that walks, rolls, picks things up, and gets back up when knocked over, controlled by a gamepad or its own trained AI.
buyer: A robotics hobbyist, STEM educator, or research lab that wants an affordable, hackable walking robot to teach or experiment on without building hardware from scratch.
business_use_cases: A university robotics course buys a fleet of these as an affordable, open platform for teaching reinforcement learning and control instead of expensive research robots.
A STEM education company builds a curriculum and robot-kit bundle around it for schools and after-school programs.
A robotics YouTuber or influencer builds a content business around customizing, racing, or teaching with the duck, selling add-on parts or tutorials to the community.

money_ideas.idea: Sell curated educational kits (duck + lesson plans + custom parts) to schools and STEM programs.
Sell premium pre-trained behavior packs (tricks, games, new RL policies) as add-on content for owners.

steal_this: Buy the duck, build a 5-lesson 'teach a robot to walk' curriculum for middle schoolers, and sell it as a weekend STEM workshop kit.
